crossRefs.note: He who robs his father and drives away his mother, is a son who causes shame and brings reproach.
He said to his mother, “The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse…
For God commanded, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to…
Whoever keeps the law is a wise son; but he who is a companion of gluttons shames his father.
One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
One who is slack in his work is brother to him who is a master of destruction.

translations.web: Whoever robs his father or his mother and says, “It’s not wrong,” is a partner with a destroyer.
translations.bsb: He who robs his father or mother, saying, “It is not wrong,” is a companion to the man who destroys.
translations.kjv: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer.
translations.asv: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression, The same is the companion of a destroyer.
